chapters.title: PRELUDE
chapters.summary: Mandelbrot is introduced as an independent scientific maverick whose fractal geometry discoveries challenge established financial theory with controversial but important insights about market risk.

chapters.title: Risk, Ruin, and Reward
chapters.summary: Financial markets are extremely risky with seemingly impossible events like the 1987 crash occurring regularly, revealing fundamental flaws in standard probability models that dramatically underestimate real market dangers.

chapters.title: By the Toss of a Coin or the Flight of an Arrow?
chapters.summary: Financial markets can be described using probability theory despite seeming deterministic, but require understanding different types of randomness beyond the familiar bell curve patterns.

chapters.title: Bachelier and His Legacy
chapters.summary: Louis Bachelier's 1900 doctoral thesis laid the foundations of modern financial theory by applying probability mathematics to market prices, though his work was initially dismissed and only rediscovered decades later.

chapters.title: The House of Modern Finance
chapters.summary: Modern financial theory rests on three key innovations—Markowitz's portfolio theory, Sharpe's asset pricing model, and Black-Scholes options formula—all built on Bachelier's probabilistic foundations but widely used despite fundamental flaws.

chapters.title: The Case Against the Modern Theory of Finance
chapters.summary: Modern financial theory's fundamental assumptions about rational investors, normal price distributions, and market continuity are systematically contradicted by real market behavior and trading practices.

chapters.title: Turbulent Markets: A Preview
chapters.summary: Financial markets exhibit the same mathematical patterns as turbulent fluid flow, with intermittent bursts of high volatility followed by calm periods, requiring multifractal analysis to model accurately.

chapters.title: Studies in Roughness: A Fractal Primer
chapters.summary: Fractal geometry studies the mathematics of roughness and irregularity in nature, using scaling patterns and fractional dimensions to quantify complex structures from coastlines to financial charts.

chapters.title: The Mystery of Cotton
chapters.summary: Mandelbrot's 1963 analysis of cotton prices revealed that financial markets follow power-law scaling patterns rather than normal distributions, solving a century-old mystery of price variation through three converging mathematical insights.

chapters.title: Long Memory, from the Nile to the Marketplace
chapters.summary: Harold Hurst's discovery of long-term dependence in Nile floods reveals that financial markets have 'memory' where past events continue to influence present price movements over extended periods.

chapters.title: Noah, Joseph, and Market Bubbles
chapters.summary: Financial markets exhibit two forms of wildness—the Noah Effect (abrupt price jumps) and Joseph Effect (long-term trends)—which interact to create rational bubbles through overshooting and crash dynamics.

chapters.title: The Multifractal Nature of Trading Time
chapters.summary: Multifractal models capture financial market behavior by deforming time itself—expanding during dramatic price changes and contracting during quiet periods—to generate realistic price charts.

chapters.title: Ten Heresies of Finance
chapters.summary: Mandelbrot challenges ten fundamental assumptions of modern finance, arguing that markets are turbulent, discontinuous, and far riskier than conventional theory suggests.

chapters.title: In the Lab
chapters.summary: Current fractal finance experiments include Olsen's currency trading platform, Bouchaud's statistical arbitrage funds, and various academic research projects, though practical applications remain limited.
